teaser.text: Domino’s is a pizza brand, a restaurant network and a food distributor at once. To understand how a dollar moves through it, start with what a customer buys, then follow the payments among stores, franchisees and the company.

stock.opening: Domino’s weighted value is $378.17 in October 2029, with a +37% return including dividends. It hinges on refinancing and franchisee economics keeping cash generation durable.
stock.closing: The full Domino’s memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Weighted value is $319.21 in October 2027. That implies +11%, including dividends. The final weighted value is $378.17 in October 2029. Its return is +37%, including dividends. The bear case probability is 27%. The base case is 53%, and the bull case is 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Domino’s?

paragraphs.text: Before July 2027, refinancing rate and terms will determine cash available to owners. Through 2027, customer baskets and franchisee returns must recover enough to support store openings. The bull case needs repeat profitable orders, improving franchisee returns and productive openings. Domino’s is ultimately a bet that healthy franchisees can keep converting orders into cash before the debt comes due.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Domino’s really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending remains necessary even in a franchised system because Domino’s must maintain technology, supply-chain facilities and company stores. The accounts do not cleanly separate maintenance spending from growth spending. Stock compensation adds another qualification: subtracting $44.6 million of stock pay leaves analytical “real free cash flow” of $626.9 million.

dividend.title: Domino’s dividend: payout and coverage
dividend.meta_description: Domino’s pays a growing dividend from positive free cash flow, but refinancing and franchisee economics could affect future payments.
dividend.opening: Domino’s pays $1.99 per quarter, or $7.96 annualized. Its 2025 free cash flow was $671.5 million and real free cash flow was $626.9 million, while recent free cash flow remained positive.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Domino’s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Domino’s pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The latest declared rate is $1.99 per quarter. It annualizes to $7.96. The base case gives dividends per share of $8.56 in the first forecast window. It rises to $9.42 and then $10.36. The bear case holds dividends at $7.96 throughout. The bull case gives $8.76, $10.07 and $11.58.

blocks.heading: Does Domino’s dividend come from free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash after capital spending. In 2025, operating cash of $792.1 million less capital spending of $120.6 million left $671.5 million, above net income. That supports the quality of the reported earnings, but not necessarily their permanence.

Capital spending remains necessary even in a franchised system because Domino’s must maintain technology, supply-chain facilities and company stores. The accounts do not cleanly separate maintenance spending from growth spending. Stock compensation adds another qualification: subtracting $44.6 million of stock pay leaves analytical “real free cash flow” of $626.9 million.

paragraphs.text: The clearest bear trigger is refinancing before July 2027. Higher interest expense would reduce net income, free cash flow and repurchase capacity.

The base case would gain support if management delivered its restrained sales and store outlook while operating income continued to grow. A completed refinancing at manageable rates would also preserve the assumed moderate buyback and dividend paths.
